major_concerns: Deterministic verifier coverage may omit vendor-specific features, biasing comparisons.
Synthetic benchmark generalizability to production multi‑vendor networks is uncertain.
Prompt sensitivity and single‑model dependence could confound effect attribution.
Blast‑radius and regression definitions need exact operational semantics and thresholds.
Power/sample‑size justification for the paired design not specified.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register exact verifier (version/feature set), document known coverage gaps and plan for handling unsupported features.
Include multiple LLM seeds and at least two model families to test generality; report prompt templates and seeds.
Precisely define blast‑radius and regression metrics (operational mapping) and preregister thresholds.
Perform verifier false‑positive/false‑negative measurement and report how these affect outcomes.
Provide statistical power calculation and justify 200 tasks or adjust sample size; preregister analysis plan and strata.

major_concerns: Adversarial‑intent generator may overfit to the target LLM, limiting external validity.
Publishing attack artifacts risks misuse; ethical disclosure and redaction policy absent.
Verifier false‑positive rates could inflate apparent mitigation effectiveness.
Need clear definition of what constitutes an "unsafe change" and blast‑radius thresholds.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register adversarial generation procedures (templates, transformations) and include multiple LLMs/prompt seeds to test transferability.
Define and preregister ethical safeguards; commit to high‑level attack taxonomy only in public artifacts (no exploitable scripts).
Measure and report verifier false positives/negatives alongside mitigation efficacy.
Preregister sample sizes and perform power analysis; specify how ambiguous intent labels are adjudicated.
Specify simulated environment details (sandbox configuration) and ensure no live credentials or networks are used.

major_concerns: Severity proxy is simulated and may not map to operator judgement or real outage impact.
Rollback‑complexity is underspecified and may be difficult to measure consistently.
Composite weighting scheme can be tuned post‑hoc unless preregistered.
Dependence on verifier fidelity may bias component metrics.
required_design_repairs: Preregister composite weighting and threshold selection protocol (avoid post‑hoc fitting).
Operationalize rollback‑complexity with a measurable procedure (e.g., config diff steps) and document measurement process.
Validate the severity proxy against a small set of human expert labels or documented incident templates (even simulated) and report concordance.
Include sensitivity/ablation analyses for each component metric and multiple LLM/prompt seeds to assess robustness.
Document verifier limitations and quantify how verifier coverage affects component values.

major_concerns: Emulated human‑approval (conservative approver) may not reflect real operator behavior; results sensitive to approver thresholds and modeled delays.
Synthetic approver delay and cost model choices are subjective and can drive conclusions.
Rollback incidence measurement and its mapping to operational cost are not fully specified.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register approver rules, thresholds, and fixed delay parameters; justify choices and include preplanned sensitivity analyses.
Define rollback detection, measurement, and costs concretely; preregister the cost metric combining time and safety.
Include multiple approver threshold settings in the preregistered plan to show robustness of tradeoffs.
Run experiments with multiple LLM seeds/models and report per‑model results; include paired design or blocking to control variance.
Provide power analysis for the 240‑task bank or adjust sample size accordingly and preregister statistical tests.
